verdict.rationale: Isaac Sim's own docs cover the whole workflow: import robots from URDF, MJCF, CAD or USD, simulate with PhysX or Newton, add RTX and physics-based sensors, and assemble scenes with materials, physics, and robot and sensor models. It also supports software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop evaluation before deployment. One community report describes sim-to-real drift from GPU execution-order effects in complex scenarios across engines, which tempers confidence in fidelity but does not concretely refute the capability. Missing for 10: detailed docs on specific sensor model types and their fidelity (e.g., lidar/IMU noise models), independent hands-on corroboration of physics realism, and resolution of the reported sim-to-real drift in complex contact scenarios.

support.subject: As a robotics engineer, I can simulate my robot and its environment with realistic physics and sensor models before touching hardware
